units.hold_A, hold_B, hold_Z, hold_L, hold_R,: bits of native button_hold after the R -> A+Z fold (0 / 1); never a scalar word
units.tap_x, tap_y: native tap counter: 1 -> 1.0, 2 -> 0.75, 3 -> 0.5, 4..253 -> 0.25, 254 -> 0 (outside the band or forced stale); 0 -> 0 and counted as an anomaly (impossible per source)
units.z_out: 1 iff tics_since_last_z > 10 (outside the Z-cancel window, incl. the 65536 reset)
units.anim_frame: clip(GObj anim_frame, 0, 240) / 60 (animation frames; frozen in hitlag)
units.aerial_lag_armed: 1 iff motion_flag1 != 0 and the status id is an aerial attack (nFTCommonStatusAttackAir*); 0 in every other status by definition

projectiles.rows: sticky slots; a weapon keeps its slot for its life; a new spawn takes the lowest free slot in ascending spawn serial; with no free slot it is dropped and counted (info v3_projectile_overflow)
projectiles.ownership: the agent's own weapons only (owner == the player fighter)
projectiles.velocity: native WPStruct vel_air (no estimate): unaffected by creation / destruction

targets.units: dx, dy: native units / 2000; vx, vy: (position - previous reply's position) / 50, 0 at reset, on a row's first live reply and on a stale reply

masks.rule: a row whose validity column is 0 is all zeros at the network input (no normalisation can move it)

segments.order: native collision line id, then vertex-pair index
segments.padding: slots >= count: every geometry and kind value 0
segments.accepts: any table with <= 32 segments (the pinned Mario table is a task validation, not a contract term)
segments.mario_reference: TopN (position_x, position_y) of the paired observation
segments.world_vertex_rule: float32 stored vertex + float32 group translate when the group is translated (mpCollisionGetVertexPositionID)

contract.stale_rule: native live = 0 or fighter invalid (the terminal reply of a fall): the last complete observation is repeated and info['v4_stale'] is true
contract.displacement_rule: agent disp_* = TopN change since the previous reply / velocity scale; 0 at reset

character.rule: status ids are looked up in the task character's own table; ids outside it map to 'unmapped' and are counted (info v4_unmapped_status_ids)
